provenance.method: Practical Scotland adult-autism assessment route assembled from current NHS inform guidance. National information is kept separate from local NHS-board service rules; no personalised diagnosis is made.

question: How do I start looking into an adult autism assessment in Scotland?
why_it_matters: A national information page can explain the starting point, but the actual assessment pathway and waiting arrangements are delivered through local NHS Scotland services.
current_understanding: NHS inform advises young people and adults in Scotland who think they may be autistic and would benefit from diagnosis to contact their GP practice. The local service then determines the operational pathway. Assessment is intended to consider lifelong patterns and their impact rather than treating an online questionnaire as diagnosis. Exact referral forms, eligibility, waiting times, private-report acceptance and post-assessment support can differ by NHS board and service. England Right to Choose is not a Scottish entitlement. ND Oracle does not decide from symptoms or screening results whether a person is autistic or whether they should seek diagnosis.
evidence_needed: Current NHS-board adult autism referral, waiting, private-report and post-assessment support evidence across Scotland.
reopening_conditions: NHS inform materially changes Scotland adult autism diagnosis guidance.
A national Scottish referral or commissioning pathway is introduced.
dissent: Formal diagnosis can be useful for some people and unnecessary, inaccessible or unwanted for others; support needs can exist before or without diagnosis.
